Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5271; undissembled, i.e. sincere:--without dissimulation (hypocrisy), unfeigned.
BiblicalUsage: Unfeigned, without hypocrisy, sincere and undisguised. Paul speaks of unfeigned love and unfeigned faith, Peter of unfeigned love of the brethren, and James of the wisdom from above that is without partiality and without hypocrisy. The word names the love and faith that are what they seem.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe unfeigned love is the mark of real faith: love without hypocrisy, faith without acting, wisdom without partiality. Paul puts it at the head of his list of the marks of the ministry, and I hold that sincerity is not a nicety but the test of whether the faith is real.
RelatedPeople: Paul; Simon Peter; Timothy; James, Brother of Jesus
